It seems to me like if kube-proxy can't get the node IPs, then it ought to fail... Can you do look through the old PRs that resulted in the current code to figure out why we made it keep going?

Historically --bind-address was directly used as NodeIP for primary IP Family detection, and 56df70b (#91725) added detectNodeIP which fetched NodeIP from Node API if the --bind-address was unspecified and fall backed to localhost on failure.
0df4a69 added the polling to wait for NodeIPs to be available with Node object, but never returned any error on poll timeout.

So, I guess the reason we ignore errors is because the node IP is mostly not actually used, other than for deciding the primary IP family, so it seemed weird to make a GetNodeHostIPs failure be fatal... But at the same time, it really should be fatal...
Either way, I dislike the fact that we completely throw the error away within NodeManager. If we're going to ignore the error, it ought to be done at the cmd/kube-proxy level.
And actually, the current code doesn't work anyway; kubelet always sets some node IPs on the node when it first creates the Node object, so the only way we could get to the end of newNodeManager without having found node IPs would be if we didn't even find a Node, in which case we'd end up setting n.node to nil and then n.NodeIPs() would crash inside utilnode.GetNodeHostIPs().
At this point we have basically normalized the fact that kube-proxy will exit and expect to be restarted in some circumstances. We should just treat the lack of a Node object as a fatal error and exit.

rawNodeIPs can be nil/empty here if it timed out, right? We need to log an error somewhere if that happens; even if it's not fatal, it's unexpected and possibly bad, so we should warn the user.
One possibility would be to log it from within NewNodeManager. Another would be to have s.NodeManager.NodeIPs() return ([]net.IP, error), and we can log the error, but then keep going.
Also (and this is a problem with the existing code), it's weird that we log rawNodeIPs but then we don't log anything if s.NodeIPs ends up being different from that...
So:

if we got no rawNodeIPs, log an error/warning
otherwise, log the rawNodeIPs (as above).
if s.NodeIPs[s.PrimaryIPFamily].IsLoopback(), log a warning about that (we do this in detectNodeIPs)
otherwise, if we used bindAddress to override rawNodeIPs, log the resulting NodeIPs

and probably that should either all be done here, or else all be done in detectNodeIPs, rather than splitting it up and making it hard to see for sure what gets logged

rawNodeIPs can be nil/empty here if it timed out, right? We need to log an error somewhere if that happens;

rawNodeIPs will never be nil, assuming kubelet always sets some node IPs on the node when it first creates the Node object.
If the node manager times out waiting for existence of node object then it will throw an error that will cause kube-proxy to fail.
In the current code s.NodeManager.NodeIPs() will never be called when node manager times out.

I wouldn't go any finer time.Millisecond. Also, you should scale things so you don't need to use fractions or express different intervals with different base units. So maybe 10 * time.Millisecond for the poll time and 15 * time.Millisecond for the sleep here.
